meta.title: Turkish Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 483 expressions · 118 everyday, 304 idioms, 61 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 483 Turkish set phrases, idioms and proverbs, in three subdecks: 118 everyday phrases, 304 idioms and 61 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Turkish → English (see the Turkish, recall the meaning) and English → Turkish (see an English meaning, recall the Turkish) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Turkish A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is an inventory of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the five, so the two can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the set phrases Wiktionary does not mark as idiomatic — mostly the everyday formulas a Turkish speaker uses as one piece (değil mi, teşekkür ederim, ne demek …), with a few sayings it files the same way. 43 of them occur in the example dialogues of the Turkish as a Foreign Language Teaching Programme (Türkiye Maarif Foundation, 2020), the syllabus the level decks are scoped by. The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (görmezden gelmek, göz atmak, can atmak …), and the PROVERBS complete sayings with a moral (hatasız kul olmaz, vakit nakittir, bir elin nesi var iki elin sesi var …). Within each subdeck the expressions are ordered by how often they occur in Tatoeba's Turkish sentences, an expression ending in a verb being counted in any form of that verb, so the ones met most often come first. Real example sentences come with 281 of the 483 expressions, three apiece for 140, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Expressions, meanings and the idiom and proverb labels: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences and the order: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
